record.context_brief: Finite-energy condition for entire GL solutions
record.original_question: Let u:R^2→R^2 be a smooth solution of Δu=u(1-|u|^2) on R^2 such that |u(x)|→1 as |x|→∞. Must u automatically satisfy the finite-potential-energy condition ∫_{R^2}(|u|^2-1)^2<∞?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.5 ([25, Problem 2], [13, Open Problem 2]). Assume that u satisfies (2.4) and (2.5). Does (2.7) hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $u:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth solution of the Ginzburg–Landau system
$$\Delta u = u\,(|u|^2-1)\qquad\text{on }\mathbb{R}^2,$$
(equivalently $-\Delta u = u(1-|u|^2)$), and assume that
$$|u(x)|\to 1\qquad\text{as }|x|\to\infty.$$
Must $u$ automatically satisfy the finite-potential-energy condition
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\bigl(|u(x)|^2-1\bigr)^2\,dx<\infty\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up any resolution of this question. Recent works on entire planar Ginzburg–Landau solutions still treat the finite-potential-energy assumption as an independent hypothesis, and the recent paper "On Brezis' First Open Problem: A Complete Solution" addresses a different problem (Brezis–Nirenberg on the 3-ball). The implication "$|u|\to 1$ at infinity $\Rightarrow$ $\int(|u|^2-1)^2<\infty$" for entire $\mathbb{R}^2$ solutions appears to remain open.
